articles.title: We built CursiveLines: learn cursive one letter at a time
articles.excerpt: Cursive is a skill a lot of adults come back to. They want to help a child with homework, read an old family letter, or sign their name with a little more confidence. The hard part isn't the shape of…
articles.body: Cursive is a skill a lot of adults come back to. They want to help a child with homework, read an old family letter, or sign their name with a little more confidence. The hard part isn't the shape of a letter. It's the movement: where the pen starts, which way it goes, and how one letter reaches into the next. A printed chart shows the finished letter and none of that. So we built CursiveLines , a free site for learning cursive one line at a time. What the site does Every letter has numbered strokes and direction arrows, and you can play the strokes back as often as you like. A trace pad lets you follow the model with a finger, mouse or stylus, then check your tracing.

articles.title: Implied vs. Historical Volatility: Which Better Predicts Realized Volatility?
articles.excerpt: If you are building a volatility-forecasting model, one recurring design decision is whether to prioritize option-implied volatility or historical volatility. The short answer: implied volatility (IV)…
articles.body: If you are building a volatility-forecasting model, one recurring design decision is whether to prioritize option-implied volatility or historical volatility. The short answer: implied volatility (IV) is usually the stronger standalone predictor of future realized volatility (RV), but it works best when combined with historical or GARCH-based estimates. The two inputs Implied volatility comes from option prices. It represents the market’s expectation of future volatility and can update quickly as new information arrives. Historical volatility is computed from past returns. It is easy to calculate and useful because volatility tends to cluster, but it is backward-looking.

articles.title: AI agent REST API from pip install: HiveGate 0.3.1
articles.excerpt: Until last week, trying HiveGate meant cloning the repo, copying .env.example, running a setup script and starting the server from the checkout. That's fine if you want to work on HiveGate. It's a lot…
articles.body: Until last week, trying HiveGate meant cloning the repo, copying .env.example , running a setup script and starting the server from the checkout. That's fine if you want to work on HiveGate. It's a lot to ask if you only want to see whether it fits your agents. HiveGate 0.3.1, released on October 31, is the first release on PyPI. You install it as a tool, write a starter config with one command, start Postgres and Qdrant, and serve. This post walks through that path from an empty directory to an AI agent REST API with per-user sessions, a paused tool call you approve over HTTP, and a cost record for every model call. It ends with what changes when you take it off your laptop. HiveGate is an MIT-licensed FastAPI service built on Agno . You write the agent. HiveGate serves it.

articles.title: How to Show Up in Google AI Overviews: 9 Proven SEO Tactics
articles.excerpt: To show up in Google AI Overviews, write content that answers questions directly in the first few sentences, structure it with question-based headings, and support it with FAQs, fresh information and…
articles.body: To show up in Google AI Overviews, write content that answers questions directly in the first few sentences, structure it with question-based headings, and support it with FAQs, fresh information and topical authority. Google's AI does not simply repeat the top-ranked page. It reads many pages, synthesizes an answer, and cites the sources it trusts most. Here is the shift you need to understand. Traditional SEO asks: how do I rank #1? AI Overview SEO asks: how do I become the clearest, most quotable answer? That is good news for small sites. You do not need the biggest domain. You need the clearest answer. Key Takeaways The AI cites the clearest, most quotable answer, not necessarily the #1 ranked page. Answer in the first 50 words, use question headings, add TL;DR boxes and FAQs.

articles.title: The Taurid meteor shower peaks tonight — and fireballs could steal the show
articles.excerpt: The Taurid meteor shower could spawn dazzling fireballs in the coming weeks! Here's when and where to look.
articles.body: Heads up stargazers! The Taurid meteor shower is upon us, bringing multiple peaks of activity that could see spectacular shooting stars and fireballs brighten November's sky. Here's where and when to look. What is the Taurid meteor shower(s)? Every autumn, Earth plows through streams of debris left behind by Comet Encke, a 3-mile-wide (4.8-kilometer) ice body that orbits the sun once every 3.3 years. These debris streams produce two branches of the Taurid meteor shower : The Southern Taurids, active from Sept. 20 to Nov. 20 and the Northern Taurids, active from Oct. 20 to Dec. 10. As Earth plows through the debris streams, tiny particles slam into our atmosphere at 65,000 miles per hour (104,607 kilometers per hour), producing dazzling streaks of light across the night sky.
